title: Japan Clears TSMC Kumamoto for 3nm Chip Production; EUV Scarcity Caps Output at 6,000 Wafers per Month
gist: A TechTimes article relayed on SemiWiki says Japan's METI approved on October 16, 2026 a revised plan for TSMC's second Kumamoto fab to make 3nm chips from December 2028 at just 6,000 wafers per month, down 87.5% from the original 48,000 at 6nm/12nm. The author attributes the cap to scarce EUV tools from ASML (about 50-60 systems a year), details revised subsidies (second fab cut to ¥645.15 billion), and notes AI-driven 3nm demand and Japan's Rapidus parallel track.

themes.theme: Kumamoto II plan and capacity cut

insights.claim: Japan's METI formally approved on October 16, 2026 a revised production plan for TSMC's second Kumamoto fab, certifying Japan's first facility able to make 3nm logic chips.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Japan joins Taiwan and South Korea in hosting commercial 3nm production, a geopolitical and supply-chain milestone.
insights.locator: Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry formally approved

insights.claim: The original 2024 plan called for 48,000 wafers per month at 6nm and 12nm, while the approved plan calls for 6,000 wafers per month at 3nm, an 87.5% capacity reduction.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Headline volume is far smaller than originally planned, limiting near-term Japan-based supply.
insights.locator: The original plan called for 48,000 wafers per month

insights.claim: The author argues the 87.5% cut is not a setback but a direct consequence of what 3nm manufacturing requires and who makes the equipment, as the facility moves from mature-node mass production to frontier-node manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Frontier-node fabs trade volume for per-wafer investment intensity.
insights.locator: The reduction is not a sign of diminished ambition.

insights.claim: TSMC has indicated the 6,000-wafer figure is only the first phase, and capacity will expand depending on the level of additional government support.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Upside to Kumamoto II capacity depends on Japanese subsidy decisions.
insights.locator: TSMC has indicated that the 6,000-wafer figure

insights.claim: Commercial production at the second Kumamoto fab is targeted for December 2028, with JASM committed under METI conditions to ten years of operation and to increasing production if a domestic shortage occurs.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Subsidy conditions create binding operating obligations for TSMC's Japan venture.
insights.locator: Commercial production at the second Kumamoto fab

themes.theme: EUV scarcity as the binding constraint

insights.claim: 3nm requires extreme ultraviolet lithography, used on more than 20 critical layers at the 3nm node versus about 14 layers at 5nm, and only ASML makes EUV systems at commercial scale.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: ASML's monopoly and rising EUV layer counts make it a chokepoint for advanced-node capacity.
insights.locator: At 3nm, a chip requires extreme ultraviolet

insights.claim: ASML produces roughly 50 to 60 EUV systems per year, and TSMC, Samsung, Intel and Rapidus all compete for allocation from that limited production, with each tool costing more than $150 million.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: EUV supply, not demand, limits leading-edge capacity growth across foundries.
insights.locator: ASML produces roughly 50 to 60 EUV systems per year globally.

insights.claim: The 6,000 wafer-per-month figure represents what EUV tool allocation and yield ramp can support in the 2026-2028 window, given TSMC is also prioritizing Arizona Fab 21 Phase 2 and its 3nm and 2nm expansion in Taiwan.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: TSMC allocates scarce EUV tools to Taiwan and Arizona before Japan.
insights.locator: The 6,000-wafer-per-month figure represents

insights.claim: Earlier reporting cited 15,000 wafers per month when Taiwan approved the 3nm investment in March 2026, while the METI-certified plan lists 6,000; METI's documents do not explain the gap, which the author sees as consistent with a tool-availability ceiling rather than demand.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Unexplained discrepancy suggests figures could be revised upward later.
insights.locator: There was earlier reporting of a 15,000-wafer monthly figure

insights.claim: ASML's NXE EUV systems use 0.33 numerical aperture optics and generate 13.5nm light by firing a pulsed laser at liquid tin droplets more than 50,000 times per second.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Explains the complexity limiting EUV tool output.
insights.locator: ASML's EUV systems

insights.claim: METI cut the planned subsidy for Kumamoto II from ¥732 billion (about $4.6 billion) to ¥645.15 billion (about $4.1 billion) to reflect reduced initial volume.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Government support scales with approved volume.
insights.locator: METI designated the Kumamoto II plant as a subsidy recipient

insights.claim: The first Kumamoto fab's subsidy was revised from ¥476 billion to ¥409.5 billion, and total committed public support across both plants fell from ¥1.208 trillion to ¥1.055 trillion (about $6.7 billion).
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Total Japanese public commitment is lower than originally planned.
insights.locator: The first Kumamoto fab's subsidy was also revised downward

insights.claim: METI is considering increasing support for the second fab and included a subsidy request in its fiscal year 2027 preliminary budget, a process that will determine whether TSMC can raise the 6,000-wafer ceiling before mass production begins.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: FY2027 budget outcome is the catalyst for Kumamoto II scale-up.
insights.locator: METI is explicitly considering increasing its support

insights.claim: TSMC says total Kumamoto capital spending exceeds $23 billion (about ¥3.63 trillion) across both facilities.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Scale of TSMC's Japan commitment relative to government subsidy.
insights.locator: TSMC's own statement confirmed total Kumamoto capital spending

themes.theme: Kumamoto I and the demand mix

insights.claim: The October 16 approval also revises Kumamoto I: it drops 12-16nm production and concentrates on 22-28nm (plus 40nm for Japanese domestic customers) at 45,000 wafers per month across the subsidized footprint and 50,000 across the full plant, versus 55,000 combined originally.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Mature-node capacity at Kumamoto I is trimmed and refocused.
insights.locator: METI's October 16 approval package extended

insights.claim: JASM attributes the Kumamoto I revision to evolving automotive and industrial demand, which the author reads as an implicit acknowledgment that sluggish electric vehicle adoption moderated demand for advanced-mature nodes.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: EV weakness is a read-through to demand for mature-node auto chips; this is the author's interpretation.
insights.locator: JASM attributes this revision to how automotive

insights.claim: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake on July 28, 2026 halted JASM Fab 1 for equipment inspections, with analysts estimating a one-week shutdown could mean about $14 million in lost revenue; the fab later returned to normal operations.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Seismic risk is a recurring concentration risk for Japanese fabs.
insights.locator: The first fab has been operating since late 2024

themes.theme: Why 3nm and AI drive the node move

insights.claim: TSMC's N3 delivers 70% logic density over 5nm, a 15% performance gain at the same transistor count and a 30% power reduction compared to 5nm.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Density and efficiency gains underpin AI accelerator demand for 3nm.
insights.locator: A 3nm chip is not merely a faster version

insights.claim: For AI workloads, transistor density and power efficiency are the primary engineering constraints, making 3nm the node at which AI accelerators cross from constrained to capable.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: AI demand sustains leading-edge node pull-through.
insights.locator: For AI workloads

insights.claim: TSMC CEO C.C. Wei met Prime Minister Takaichi in Tokyo in February 2026, citing 'strong demand driven by AI' for moving the second Kumamoto fab from 6nm to 3nm.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: AI demand is the stated driver for upgrading Japan's fab node.
insights.locator: TSMC CEO C.C. Wei met Prime Minister Takaichi

insights.claim: By installing 3nm capacity in Japan, TSMC can serve GPU and AI accelerator customers who need geographically diversified supply chains and capture Japanese hyperscaler and defense-adjacent demand.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Supply-chain diversification is a selling point for non-Taiwan 3nm capacity.
insights.locator: By installing 3nm capacity in Japan

insights.claim: TSMC holds 86.5% of JASM, with Sony Semiconductor Solutions at 6%, Denso at 5.5% and Toyota at about 2%.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Japanese industrial partners have direct stakes in the outcome.
insights.locator: JASM's ownership structure

insights.claim: Outside Taiwan and South Korea no country currently hosts commercial 3nm production, so Kumamoto II makes Japan a participant, initially modest, in frontier logic for the first time since the 1980s.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Geographic spread of leading-edge logic is changing slowly and modestly.
insights.locator: The approval places Japan in a position

insights.claim: Japan also backs Rapidus, targeting 2nm mass production in Hokkaido in the second half of 2027; METI calls it complementary to TSMC Kumamoto, targeting smaller volumes, faster cycle times and domestic design houses.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Two-track strategy: Rapidus for agility and TSMC for volume.
insights.locator: Japan is simultaneously backing Rapidus Corp.

insights.claim: Kumamoto II's 3nm comes online about one year after TSMC's second Arizona fab (targeting 3nm in the second half of 2027), reflecting TSMC's capital allocation priorities of Taiwan first, then Arizona under CHIPS Act pressure, then Japan.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Japan is third in line for TSMC's leading-edge capital.
insights.locator: The 2028 production date means Kumamoto's 3nm node

insights.claim: At 6,000 wafers per month Kumamoto II will not meaningfully close the gap with AI silicon demand expected to exceed supply well into the next decade; the real engineering work is qualifying the Japanese site to Taiwan's yield standards.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Don't expect Kumamoto II to relieve AI chip supply tightness; yield qualification is the risk.
insights.locator: For the global AI chip supply chain

insights.claim: Arizona's 3nm capacity at ramp is approximately 10,000-20,000 wafers per month, while Taiwan's Fabs 18A, 18B and 18C in Tainan handle the majority of global 3nm logic demand from Nvidia, Apple and AMD.
insights.speaker: Levi Kohler
insights.so_what: Taiwan remains the dominant 3nm source; overseas fabs are small by comparison.
insights.locator: How does Kumamoto II compare to TSMC's other 3nm facilities?
